access.edition_or_version: Gita Press, Gorakhpur editions; Avadhi text with Hindi commentary

mechanics.premise: A vernacular retelling of the Rama story as an act of devotion, moving through narrative episodes toward the establishment of devotion (bhakti) as the goal.
mechanics.reader_promise: Devotional participation in a sacred narrative whose rhythms are designed for recitation and communal hearing.
mechanics.point_of_view: A devotional narrator who addresses Ram directly and invites the audience into the narration.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Alternating doha and chaupai metres; refrain and parallel verse; vocative invocation of the deity as narrative frame.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Invocation -> sacred narrative -> crises and separations -> the triumph of devotion and grace.
mechanics.sacred_or_profound_object: Ram, addressed and invoked as a present divine lord rather than narrated as a distant figure.
mechanics.devotional_or_apophatic_mode: Devotional (saguna) with direct vocative address; the sacred is personal and named.
mechanics.cadence_and_form: Avadhi devotional metre built for recitation; ring structure framing the narrative with praise.
mechanics.figuration: Analogy and devotional comparison drawn from everyday Awadhi life; repetition as liturgical structure.
mechanics.vocative_address: Opening and closing invocations address the deity; devotion is grammatically directed.
mechanics.cultural_scope: North Indian Vaishnava bhakti; a vernacular challenge to Sanskrit literary monopoly, historically recited across social strata.
mechanics.translation_notes: Metre, refrain, and Avadhi idiom are not recoverable in English translation; claims here are structural (vocative frame, ritual repetition).
mechanics.copyright_note: Techniques described, never quoted; modern editions/translations copyrighted.
